title: Auditor prep — Socratic debrief and RBAC/Audit-log synthesis
content:
Purpose and audience:
This working debrief is a compact, Socratic-style prep pack for auditors and internal reviewers covering RBAC v2, audit-log schema decisions, SIEM export expectations, and evidence automation touchpoints for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control mapping. Primary audience: internal security leads, SREs responsible for logging/export pipelines, and the external audit team.

Scope & constraints:
- Focus: controls related to access controls (AC), logging & monitoring (LM), change management (CM), and evidence retention.
- Excluded: physical security controls, vendor contract legalese (separate binder).
- This is a draft — contains proposed answers and pointers to automated evidence; assume one week buffer before final audit dry-run.

High-level control mapping summary (plain language):
- AC (Access Control): RBAC v2 enforces role-based permissions at the API gateway and service mesh level. Roles are defined centrally and synced to downstream services via the RBAC service. Evidence paths: role schema, role change audit log, user-role assignment snapshots, policy rollouts.
- LM (Logging & Monitoring): All auth events, token issuance/refresh, policy evaluation outcomes, and access denials are emitted to the audit log stream and forwarded to SIEM with the standardized JSON schema. Evidence paths: raw log archives (S3), SIEM export rules, sample queries and alert definitions.
- CM (Change Management): Role and policy changes are tied to Git commits and deployment pipelines (PR link + CI artifact). Evidence: Git history, PR approvals, deployment audit events.

Socratic Q&A (auditor-facing):
Q: How do you prove the role that allowed an access decision existed at the time of the event?
A: We timestamp role version snapshots at every rollout. The policy engine emits a policy_version_id with each access decision. Evidence to show: (a) access decision log line with policy_version_id, (b) snapshot file for that version in archive (key: roles/snapshots/roles-<version>.json), (c) PR and changelog that produced <version>.

Q: Show me a random sample of failed access attempts for the last 30 days. How do you ensure sampling is representative?
A: SIEM sampling job (siem/sampling/failure-sampler) performs stratified sampling by service and user_type. Steps: run query in SIEM for outcome:denied AND event_type:auth, apply stratification by service, output 50 samples. Evidence: saved SIEM query, sampling script runbook, CSV export.

Q: Could an engineer modify the audit log format and break ingestion without detection?
A: Modifying the schema requires a change to the central logging library (repo: logging-core). Any PR that changes the schema triggers a CI check that runs a small ingestion verification job against the staging SIEM endpoint. Evidence: PR with failing/passing CI, CI job logs, deployment event to staging. Also we have an alert if ingestion error rate rises >1% in 5 minutes.

Gap analysis (concise):
Identified gaps (high-priority first):
1) Evidence retention latency: snapshots for role definitions currently archive on a nightly batch; auditors want near-real-time snapshotting for critical changes. Impact: ability to tie instantaneous role state to an access event. Remediation: add immediate versioned snapshot on role-change webhook (owner: eng-platform, ETA: 3 sprints).
2) SIEM mapping docs: field-level mappings between audit-log keys and SIEM fields are partially documented; missing edge-case transformations (e.g., nested policy_reason). Impact: manual translation during audits. Remediation: publish mapping doc and automated transformer tests (owner: observability team, ETA: 2 weeks).
3) Evidence stitching for delegated access (service-to-service impersonation): currently logs show caller_id and subject_id but not the full delegation chain when a token was minted via another service. Impact: auditors request explicit delegation chain for high-privilege invocations. Remediation: extend audit log to include delegation_chain field and backfill for high-risk events (owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 4 sprints).

Low-priority gaps:
- Retention labeling on archived exports (cosmetic, low risk).
- Consistency of examples in runbook and PR templates.

Prioritized remediation plan (milestones and owners):
- Week 1: Publish SIEM mapping doc; add unit tests for transformer (obs team).
- Week 2–6: Implement immediate role-version snapshot webhook + archival path (eng-platform).
- Sprint 3–4: Add delegation_chain to audit schema and roll out consumer changes with canary (serving-runtime + observability).
- Pre-audit dry-run (2 weeks before audit): run auditor simulation runbook and produce evidence bundle.

SIEM export & audit-log schema (practical checklist):
- Minimum fields required per control: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_type, service, action, resource, outcome, policy_version_id, request_id, correlation_id, host, region, delegation_chain(optional).
- Recommended field types: timestamp=ISO8601; ids=uuid strings; outcome=enum (allowed/denied/error); policy_version_id=semantic string.
- Compression & transport: logs uploaded to S3 then ingested by SIEM via SQS notification and batch connector; live-forwarding uses kafka topic audit-log-live.
- Export checks: checksum per upload, manifest file, retention policy tag (retention: 365d for SOC2 evidence).

Audit simulation scenarios (what we will run during dry-run):
1) Role change replay: pick a role change PR, run the webhook snapshot, then query a corresponding access event and show attached snapshot and PR.
2) False-positive sampling: intentionally generate 100 denied events from test harness and validate that sampling excludes synthetic test tokens (we'll include a test_token flag in metadata).
3) Ingestion-break test: merge a safe schema change into a feature branch and run CI ingestion smoke test to show CI gate prevents accidental breakage.

Evidence bundle layout (what the auditor will receive):
- manifest.md (list of items + short description)
- logs/: zipped log exports (timeboxed) + manifest checksums
- snapshots/: role snapshots (by version)
- git/: PRs and commit links that created role versions
- siem_queries/: saved queries + csv exports
- runbooks/: sampling runbook + ingestion-runbook

Quick examples (cut‑and‑paste for auditor):
- SIEM query (plain): event_type:auth AND outcome:denied AND timestamp:[2025-02-01 TO 2025-02-28] | sort by timestamp desc | limit 500
- Access decision log line (example JSON, single-line in log): {"ts":"2025-02-14T10:12:03Z","event_id":"a1b2c3","actor_id":"user:alice","service":"model-host","action":"request.generate","resource":"model:ggml-13b","outcome":"denied","policy_version_id":"roles-v2025-02-14-3","request_id":"r-98765"}

Auditor-facing checklist (one page):
- Show one access decision and corresponding role snapshot (policy_version_id match).
- Show Git PR that introduced policy change and CI result.
- Export 50 denied auth events and demonstrate sampling method.
- Demonstrate rollback policy and canary fallback of policy service (show metrics during a simulated rollback).
- Provide archived SIEM export with manifest and checksums.

Known risks and caveats to communicate to auditors:
- Backfilled/delegation_chain data will be partial until rollout completes; we will annotate any backfilled records in the manifest.
- Nightly-only snapshots are acceptable for lower-risk controls but auditors will escalate for critical role changes if snapshots are nightly.

Next steps (immediate action items):
- Obs: finalize SIEM field mapping doc and attach to confluence (action owner: Rosa Kim, due: 2025-02-21).
- Platform: add role-change webhook to snapshot pipeline and drop a design PR (owner: Diego Alvarado, due: 2025-03-12).
- Security lead: schedule dry-run and provide auditor checklist (owner: Maya Patel, due: 2025-03-20).

Notes to self: keep this short during audit walk-through; focus on two stories (1. role-change -> decision tie, 2. ingestion safety via CI). Save deep-dive details for follow-up sessions.

Appendix (links & artifacts to attach to evidence bundle):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/221
- CI artifact: ci.redwood.net/builds/4123/logs
- JIRA ticket: SEC-4123 (role-versioning enhancement)
- Confluence: RBAC v2 design spec (conf-RBACv2-2024)

End of draft.
